This completeness is essential for defining bounded linear functionals, which are central to dual space theory. The Riesz representation theorem asserts that every bounded linear functional on L2 corresponds uniquely to an element in L2 itself, enabling integration against a measure. This duality underpins both probabilistic inference (via Radon-Nikodym derivatives) and dynamic system modeling (via state transitions). The failure mode arises when functionals lack boundedness or when the underlying measure lacks sufficient regularity. These structures form the bedrock of modern functional analysis and inform GSI’s Bayesian updating and GSE’s state evolution mechanisms.
